item.title: El Banco Central de Perú aclara los límites contractuales de los adquirentes, pero expertos prevén retos en cláusulas de permanencia
item.description: El Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCRP) dictó una norma para regular el servicio de aceptación de pagos que prohíbe cláusulas que restrinjan a los comercios la contratación de otros aceptadores de pagos. La norma, que entrará en vigor el 1 de enero de 2027, tampoco permite establecer tarifas o descuentos especiales que incentiven el uso exclusivo de un solo aceptador. 0026-2026-BCRP, el regulador busca que exista libertad para elegir con cuáles proveedores trabajar, mientras deja un margen de negociación acotado para los aceptadores.

item.title: Celia Castañs (Tributos) sustituye a Jorge Alberto Ferreras en el Consejo del Consorcio
item.description: El Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa ha nombrado a Celia Castañs García , subdirectora general de Tributación de las Operaciones Financieras de la Dirección General de Tributos, como vocal del Consejo de Administración del Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros, en sustitución de Jorge Alberto Ferreras Gutiérrez , cuyo cese también se ha publicado en el BOE. Por su parte, Ferreras fue nombrado en marzo de este año director general de Tributos del Ministerio de Hacienda. Castañs fue nombrada subdirectora general de Tributación de las Operaciones Financieras el pasado mes de septiembre, después de ejercer como coordinadora de área en el mismo departamento.

item.title: Sabseg compra la correduría MecVis en su objetivo de ser líder del middle market italiano
item.description: Como adelantó su CEO, Eduardo Dávila , en la entrevista concedida a las publicaciones de INESE a principios de año, Sabseg tiene al mercado italiano en su foco de crecimiento para este año dentro de su objetivo de convertirse en el bróker de referencia en el mercado de intermediación de seguros del Sur de Europa, con más de 2.000 millones de primas intermediadas, antes de 2030 . De esta forma, tras las incorporaciones de Asigest, Today e Insurance Solutions, se sabe ya su cuarta compra en el mercado transalpino: la correduría Mec.Vis S.r.l., especializada en el asesoramiento y la gestión de riesgos empresariales . La operación le permite a Sabseg ampliar su presencia en el noreste de Italia, con implantación en Trentino-Alto Adigio y nuevas oportunidades de desarrollo en el Véneto .

item.title: La resiliencia climática debe ser una prioridad económica, no solo medioambiental
item.description: Según la federación, el aumento de las pérdidas vinculadas al clima en Europa obliga a tratar la resiliencia como una prioridad económica, además de medioambiental. Insurance Europe considera que el Marco de Resiliencia Climática presentado ayer por la Comisión Europea es un paso para reforzar la preparación de Europa ante el cambio climático, pero pide que la prevención, la adaptación y la responsabilidad compartida ocupen el centro de la iniciativa. Insurance Europe defiende integrar la resiliencia en la toma de decisiones de las políticas públicas.

item.title: Guidewire Extends Core Platform for Agentic Insurance
item.description: Guidewire (San Mateo, Calif.) has announced its introduction of a broader platform approach to agentic insurance, bringing AI agents onto the same core platform used for policy, billing and claims operations. “By embedding agentic capabilities where insurers already run their core operations, Guidewire gives agents the context and controls they need to work with speed and precision on a proven durable foundation.” Guidewire says agents operating on the platform can work with an insurer’s existing data and workflows while platform controls determine what information they can access, what actions they can take and how those actions are audited. “Insurance is a business of decisions and actions made in context,” comments Mike Rosenbaum, CEO, Guidewire.

item.title: The Invisible Graph: How Companies Grow Revenue And Still Lose Value
item.description: The conversation prompted me to consider something I believe many entrepreneurs miss, and it’s this: Revenue can rise while enterprise value falls. But another graph deserves equal attention: enterprise value. Revenue increased 33%, while value declined 22%.

item.title: RenRe raised $150m for new Lighthouse Cat Bond Fund, reports $81.7m of Q3 fee income
item.description: RenaissanceRe, the Bermuda headquartered reinsurance company and third-party capital manager, raised $150 million of capital for a new catastrophe bond strategy in the third-quarter, with the Lighthouse Cat Bond Fund launched as a managed account sitting under its Upsilon vehicle. The Lighthouse Cat Bond Fund is the latest separately managed account established under RenaissanceRe’s Upsilon structure, as the company continues to attract investor capital to its managed insurance-linked securities strategies. Total net income attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests in the third-party capital and ILS fund strategies reached $150.7 million for the third-quarter of 2026, which RenRe said was primarily driven by strong underwriting income in both DaVinci and Vermeer, but this was partly offset by an underwriting loss in the Fontana casualty and specialty lines joint-venture.

item.title: Lockton Re names Jeremy England Lee as Chairman, Bermuda
item.description: Lockton Re, part of the independent Lockton broking group, has announced that senior reinsurance and retrocession specialist broker Jeremy England Lee is relocating to become Chairman of the firm’s Bermuda operation. Now, he is relocating to Lockton Re’s Bermuda office where he will take on the role of Chairman, as the broking group looks to further build out senior capabilities on the island and strengthen its offering there. I am incredibly proud of the strength and momentum of Lockton Re, and Bermuda continues to be a vital geography for our continued success.” England Lee added on his new role and move, “The prospect of building on the time I have spent with the team in Bermuda and working even more closely with colleagues visiting the Island and other team members including Partners based there; Tom Parcell and Ben Ryan, is both exciting and motivating.

item.title: Morocco targets regulatory framework for insurance securitization, including cat bonds
item.description: The government of Morocco is now aiming to prepare a regulatory framework to allow for the securitization of insurance risks, including through catastrophe bonds, as the country seemingly aims to support issuance as well as to be a beneficiary of risk transfer to the capital markets. The new Finance Bill for fiscal year 2027 calls for the preparation of a regulatory framework for the securitization of insurance risks, including catastrophe bonds. It’s particularly notable to see the mention of Morocco having a goal to construct its own regulatory framework for the securitization of insurance risks, as a way to bring third-party capital more directly into the country to support natural disaster, catastrophe and climate risk transfer.

item.title: S&P assigns first-time ratings to Peak Re
item.description: S&P Global Ratings has assigned a first-time A- long-term issuer credit and financial strength rating to Peak Reinsurance Company Limited (Peak Re), a Hong Kong-based global reinsurer, with a stable outlook. Victor Kuk, Chief Executive Officer of Peak Re, commented, “We are pleased that S&P’s first rating of Peak Re is aligned with the strong financial strength ratings we hold from AM Best and Moody’s. The ratings from S&P complement Peak Re’s existing financial strength ratings of A- (Excellent) from AM Best and A3 from Moody’s.

item.title: Mapfre Re’s 9M’26 profit climbs 11.8% to €286m
item.description: Mapfre Re, Mapfre’s Reinsurance and Global Risks arm, grew profit 11.8% to €286 million in the first nine months of 2026, helped by a 67.8% rise in its Non-Life financial result, even as its combined ratio worsened and it absorbed the impact of the earthquake in Colombia. At group level, Mapfre’s net profit for the first nine months of 2026 rose 11.5% to €924 million, while total premiums grew 2% to €22.8 billion, with Life up 5% and Non-Life up 1.1%. Mapfre Re’s premiums were broadly steady at €6.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with Mapfre citing declining reinsurance and insurance rates.

item.title: Aon’s Reinsurance Solutions delivers 7% revenue growth to $572m in Q3’26
item.description: Aon’s Reinsurance Solutions business recorded organic revenue growth of 7% in the third quarter of 2026 to $572 million, driven by strong growth in treaty placements, as total revenue across the Group increased by 3% year-on-year to $4.1 billion, with organic revenue growth of 6%. In the broker’s Risk Capital division, which includes Reinsurance Solutions and Commercial Risk Solutions, revenue increased 6% year-on-year, with growth in both units. Global broking group Aon has reported a strong set of results for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, with the firm highlighting broad-based strength across solution lines, with organic revenue growth of 7% in Commercial Risk, 7% in Reinsurance, 6% in Health, and 4% in Wealth.

item.title: Wealthsimple valued at C$13.8 billion in new funding round
item.description: Canadian financial services platform Wealthsimple has agreed to an equity financing of up to C$425 million at a C$13.8 billion post-money valuation, led by GIC . The financing follows Wealthsimple’s C$750 million raise at a C$10 billion valuation in October 2025. As of September 30, Wealthsimple reported C$169.2 billion in assets under administration, up from C$100 billion at the time of its previous raise.

item.title: Slide grows profit, expands credit facility to $1.07 billion
item.description: Slide Insurance reported third-quarter net income of $138.2 million, up 24.5% from a year earlier, while entering into a new $1.07 billion credit facility and declaring a special dividend. The new credit facility, led by Huntington National Bank, replaces a $530.4 million agreement and more than doubles borrowing capacity. Slide continued expanding residential E&S business in California and homeowners offerings in South Carolina and Rhode Island.

item.title: Insurance Intake Goes Inbox-First as Canopy Connect Introduces Email Intake
item.description: Canopy Connect, the insurance intake platform used by more than 24,000 agents across more than 6,000 agencies, has added email to the ways prospects can share their insurance information. The new feature, Email Intake , lets a prospect send documents to an agent’s dedicated address and have the data show up, already structured, in the agent’s Canopy Connect dashboard. Because Email Intake produces the same structured data as the other Sharing Paths within Canopy Connect, intake stays consistent however a prospect chooses to share.

item.title: Kinro Onboards Autonomous Robotics Expert Gene Rush to Define AI Autonomy in Insurance
item.description: InsurTech startup Kinro has announced the addition of Gene Rush to its core team, leveraging his extensive background in autonomous robotics to help define operational boundaries for AI-driven insurance brokerage. According to Kinro, defining autonomy in insurance mirrors robotics engineering—it requires giving AI systems room to act independently while ensuring every decision strictly respects real-world constraints: “Autonomy doesn’t mean letting a robot do whatever it wants. Rush, who holds a PhD in autonomous robotics and previously built his own startup, spent six years engineering robots capable of independent execution.

item.title: Guidewire to Acquire hyperexponential for Up to $2.1 Billion
item.description: Guidewire (San Mateo, Calif.) has signed a definitive agreement to acquire hyperexponential (London) for $1.7 billion in cash, with up to an additional $400 million contingent on specified recurring-revenue targets. Hyperexponential provides AI-native underwriting and pricing technology for commercial P&C insurance and is already a Guidewire PartnerConnect Technology Alliance Partner. The acquisition brings together Guidewire’s core P&C platform and insurance data with hyperexponential’s capabilities spanning submission triage, risk assessment, pricing, rating and portfolio management.

item.title: Qubit and Unified Labs explore tokenized lending insurance
item.description: Qubit Underwriting and Unified Labs have partnered to develop an insurance program for lending vaults on Morpho, a decentralized finance protocol. It follows Unified Labs’ launch of GOLDX, a bank-issued tokenized gold lending market on Morpho. The collaboration will explore coverage for specified operational, technology and other agreed risks associated with institutional lending vaults backed by tokenized real-world assets.

item.title: Insurers Price Robots by the Day, Robotaxis by the Mile
item.description: Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance will sell AI robot insurance in November that pays for repairs, third-party injury and property damage claims and the wages of replacement workers or rental fees for substitute robots, with premiums about 20% above conventional industrial coverage. Lemonade charges Tesla drivers about 50% less per mile when Full Self-Driving is engaged, and Allianz Partners will supply Waymo with fleet and product liability insurance for its London and Munich launches. Self-driving cars, humanoid robots and factory automation carry risks that standard auto, property and liability policies don’t usually cover.

item.title: Korra Deal Analysis bridges gap between re/insurance and capital markets: Ledger CEO, Shah
item.description: Following the launch of Korra’s Deal Analysis platform, Samir Shah, Co-founder and CEO of Ledger Investing, the parent company of Korra, outlined during an interview with Artemis how the tool aims to bridge the long-standing gap between traditional re/insurance and capital market investors. During a recent interview with Artemis, Shah explained that the company decided to build the Korra Deal Analysis application to effectively help bridge the gap between re/insurance and the capital markets. Given this, we decided to package everything we built for internal use and launch it as a separate business for external clients.” He continued: “It’s important to distinguish though, that through Korra Analysis, the key gap that we are filling is the divide between the re/insurance markets and capital markets.

item.title: EU unveils climate resilience framework with re/insurance protection gap in focus
item.description: The European Commission has presented an EU Framework for Climate Resilience to strengthen Europe’s ability to anticipate, prepare for and manage climate risks, highlighting re/insurance as a “crucial element” in this equation. The framework reportedly aims to embed climate resilience across EU policies, support local and regional authorities, and encourage private-sector investment in adaptation, with an estimated €70 billion a year needed to adapt Europe’s infrastructure and economy. We are ensuring that climate resilience will be included in policies across the continent, supporting investment, innovation and long-term growth.” Alongside the framework, the Commission has proposed a Climate Resilience Law to establish common assumptions for future global warming, simplify national planning through a single strategic plan for each member state, and improve the consistency of climate risk assessments.

item.title: India Braces for Cyclone as El Niño Upends Global Storm Seasons
item.description: Tropical Cyclone Arnab is expected to hit India’s east coast on Wednesday, marking a break in an otherwise calm season that’s been subdued by a severe El Niño. El Niño has upended typical cyclone seasons around the world this year. “One of the key climatic events has been the suppression of the Indian monsoon and with it, the much reduced tropical cyclone activity, driven by the long reach of the El Niño,” said Christian Werner , managing director of Global Weather Climate Analytics.

item.title: Turkish Insurer Sinks as Top Executives Arrested in Fund Probe
item.description: Turkiye Sigorta AS shares extended losses after local media reported that two of its top executives were arrested as part of a sweeping probe into allegations of market manipulation in Turkish funds. Broadcaster NTV reported allegations that Turkiye Sigorta, a state-back insurance company, had steered cash into funds managed by Tera Portfoy Yonetimi, the brokerage firm at the center of the fund crisis, citing sources it did not identify. Cakmak and Ozer join a growing list of prominent figures from Turkey’s finance scene who have been arrested as authorities try to get a grip on a crisis that has battered stock and bond markets.

item.title: AI Voice Agents Transform Lead Calling
item.description: AI voice agents can now place that first call within seconds, at whatever volume the lead flow demands. An AI voice agent can call the moment a lead arrives, confirm that the person asked to be contacted, ask a few eligibility questions, and hand the live call to a licensed agent. AI can contact leads much faster than a human workforce can, boosting sales, but a small error rate in managing the AI can lead to serious problems.

item.title: Ullico leads $120 million loan for White Plains garage
item.description: Ullico has closed a $120 million construction loan as lead lender for a 1,950-space parking garage in White Plains, New York. The garage will connect to White Plains Hospital, which will lease it under a long-term agreement. First Citizen is participating in 50% of the loan.

item.title: OfficeHubb connects ChatGPT users with independent agencies
item.description: OfficeHubb has introduced a ChatGPT app that lets consumers find participating independent insurance agencies, submit quote requests and ask for help with existing policies. The app serves US agencies that use OfficeHubb’s office management platform. OfficeHubb does not generate prices, bind coverage or rank agencies and carriers.

item.title: RiverStone plans to merge Malta entity into Irish business
item.description: RiverStone International is seeking approval to merge RiverStone Insurance (Malta) Limited into RiverStone International Ireland DAC. Under the proposal, all assets and liabilities of the Malta company, including its insurance portfolio, would transfer to the Irish entity. The Malta company, including its Swiss branch, would be dissolved without going into liquidation.

item.title: JD Power: Total Loss Auto Claims Weigh Down Insurance Customer Satisfaction
item.description: Customer satisfaction with total loss auto insurance claims fell for a third straight year, while satisfaction improved for claims involving repairable vehicles, a new study looking at this year shows. Customer satisfaction with total loss claims fell 12 points on a 1,000-point scale in 2026, marking a 46-point decline since 2023, according to the JD Power 2026 U.S. Related: Report: Auto Insurance Total Loss Frequency Climbs, More Drivers Paying for Repairs Overall, 26% of auto insurance claims were classified as total losses this year, up from 16% four years ago.

item.title: GM Targets ‘Eyes-off’ Autonomous Driving Despite Liability Concerns
item.description: General Motors plans to offer “eyes-off” autonomous driving on its highest-selling, most profitable vehicles — big pickup trucks and SUVs — as it seeks fresh revenue streams from heavy technology investments. Some industry executives have said eyes-off driving that exchanges control back and forth from the car to the driver raises thorny safety and liability questions, and might not interest enough car shoppers. Last year, GM said it would offer autonomous highway driving in 2028 on its pricey but light-selling Cadillac Escalade IQ, an electric SUV.

item.title: Mayor Says Employee Error Caused Ohio Chemical Leak
item.description: Officials in northeast Ohio said Friday that a chemical tank leak earlier in the week was caused by a chemical reaction resulting from an employee error and lifted all remaining evacuation orders. The chemical leak happened when an employee of the company “introduced a temperature level to the tank in the process of trying to transfer the liquid” that caused a chemical reaction, the mayor said. Based on data that officials have seen so far, the amount of the chemical in the air didn’t reach levels high enough to have “a long-term meaningful impact on human health,” the mayor said.

item.title: Utah’s Lower, Strict Drinking Limit Resulted in Long Term Drop in Alcohol-related Crashes: IIHS
item.description: A long-term drop in alcohol-related crashes was seen after Utah imposed a stricter limit on the amount of alcohol drivers are allowed to have in their system, a new study from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety revealed. The stricter limit led to a nearly 9% reduction in alcohol-related crashes over the next four years, researchers found. state to lower the blood alcohol concentration (BAC) threshold for impaired driving to 0.05% from 0.08% in December 2018, Utah remains the only one.

item.title: Insurers lean on third-party capital, strategic partnerships to manage operating models: BlackRock
item.description: BlackRock’s 15th annual survey of the global insurance industry found that insurance capital solutions have become a critical part of how insurers manage their businesses, highlighting that third-party capital partnerships can help allocate risk and capital more effectively, while preserving the capacity to compete, invest in growth, and meet policyholder obligations. BlackRock’s survey, which includes perspectives of 463 insurers across 31 markets representing investable assets of more than $24 trillion, underscored how central partnerships are becoming to insurers’ operating models. “For property and casualty and specialty insurers, sidecars and third-party capital can provide stable underwriting capacity and help manage concentrations and peak-loss exposures.

item.title: Hannover Re collateralised fronting grows 10% in 2026. HCP plans two ILS fund strategies
item.description: Hannover Re has continued to expand its collateralised fronting business this year, growing it 10% so far in 2026 according to executives from the company. “Our other ILS offerings are catastrophe bonds transformer services, actuarial structuring for ILS Life transactions, investments in cat bonds or in private reinsurance strategies.” The collateralised reinsurance fronting offering remains a key driver of expansion in insurance-linked securities for Hannover Re, presumably driving meaningful fee income for the reinsurance company as it continues to be a key service-provider to investors and ILS market participants. While we’ve also learned that under its Hannover Re Capital Partners unit two insurance-linked securities fund strategies are planned for launch.

item.title: EU Commission proposes climate resilience framework, highlights cat bonds & reinsurance
item.description: The European Commission has called for a new climate resilience framework to strengthen Europe’s ability to anticipate, prepare for, and manage climate risks. “The EU Climate Resilience Framework aims to strengthen Europe’s ability to anticipate, prepare for, and manage climate risks by getting ahead of those impacts and avoiding damages through coordinated action at EU, national and local levels,” the Commission explained. The Framework combines a proposed European Climate Resilience Law with practical tools and supporting measures to help public authorities, businesses, and other stakeholders make better-informed decisions.” As mentioned, the proposal explains that the European Commission will set up a Climate Insurance Alliance, to help improve insurance protection and support risk prevention across Europe.

item.title: Hampden Risk Partners names Danny Milnes Head of Exposure Management
item.description: Hampden Risk Partners (HRP), an insurance business operating through Syndicate 2689 at Lloyd’s, has appointed Danny Milnes to the position of Head of Exposure Management as it continues to develop its underwriting and portfolio management capabilities. Commenting on the appointment, Leah Rose, Chief Executive Officer of Hampden Risk Partners, added: “We are delighted to welcome Danny to Hampden Risk Partners. Milnes will oversee the further development of HRP’s exposure management function, using data and analytical insights to inform underwriting decisions and support portfolio optimisation as the business pursues its growth plans.

item.title: Amynta Group completes acquisition of specialty MGU Southern States Underwriters
item.description: Amynta Group, an insurance services provider, has completed its acquisition of Southern States Underwriters and SSC Insurance Agency (collectively, Southern States Underwriters). In August 2026, Amynta Group announced that it had agreed to acquire Southern States Underwriters. Founded in 1953, Southern States Underwriters is a specialty managing general underwriter (MGU) providing commercial property and casualty insurance to the agribusiness market.

item.title: Lockton appoints Sara Romine as Executive VP, Chief Legal Officer, and Corporate Secretary
item.description: Lockton, a privately held, independent insurance brokerage, has appointed Sara Romine as Executive Vice President, Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary, with the appointment taking effect on 1 November 2026. Ron Lockton, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Lockton, commented: “Sara has earned the trust of leaders across our business through her judgement, expertise, and ability to work collaboratively.” He continued: “She is widely recognised as a top performer, and I have tremendous confidence in Sara and our legal team as we continue to grow and strengthen Lockton around the world.” Romine joined Lockton in December 2022 as Senior Vice President and US General Counsel. I couldn’t be more pleased to see Sara take it forward.” Romine said: “As Lockton continues to grow, the legal function has an increasingly important role to play in helping the business navigate complexity, seize opportunities, and support clients around the world.

item.title: People Moves: CM Vantage Appoints Finnegan as Managing Director, Casualty; Alliant Adds Sprangler to Midwest Benefits Team
item.description: Alliant Adds Karen Sprangler to Midwest Benefits Team Karen Spangler has joined Alliant Insurance Services as vice president within its employee benefits group. CM Vantage has appointed Amy Finnegan as managing director, casualty, bringing excess and surplus lines expertise and leadership to its underwriting organization. In her new role, Finnegan will lead casualty underwriting strategy and help drive profitable growth while working closely with wholesale brokers across the country.

item.title: Explosion and Fire Erupt at Quaker Oats Plant in Iowa
item.description: An apparent explosion caused a fire over the weekend at a Quaker Oats plant in Iowa that the company touts as the largest milling facility in the world. The fire evidently began with an explosion, the department said via Facebook. The Quaker Oats brand, by way of the Quaker Mill Company, turns 150 years old in 2027.

item.title: PHP Security Flaws Highlight Potential Systemic Risk Aggregation for Cyber Insurers
item.description: Recently discovered security flaws in PHP programming language, used by many websites globally, has highlighted the potential for cyber risk aggregation, which has long worried insurers and made them reluctant to aggressively increase their risk appetites, according to the ratings agency AM Best. In three separate commentaries, AM Best, cyber risk analysis firm CyberCube and Moody’s Ratings all highlighted how artificial intelligence is accelerating the discovery of such software flaws and increasing the potential for systemic cyber risks which could simultaneously hit many policyholders across the globe. Vulnerabilities affecting PHP (formally known as PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor) “could allow attackers to gain access to websites and steal sensitive information, as well as create backdoors that can let them access the sites in the future,” AM Best said in a press release announcing the publication of its commentary titled “ PHP Vulnerabilities Raises Concerns of Systemic Event for Cyber Insurers .” CyberCube explained that PHP is the software that runs the code behind roughly 70% of websites.

item.title: Brown & Brown sees 9M 2026 revenue hit $5.3bn
item.description: Brown & Brown has disclosed revenue of $5.3bn for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, up 23.4% from the same period last year. For the third quarter alone, the firm recorded revenue of $1.73bn, an increase of 7.4% on the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDAC rose 1.7% year on year to $597m in the quarter, while income before tax increased 2.9% to $320m and net income attributable to Brown & Brown grew 5.7% to $240m.

item.title: $1.7bn deal: Guidewire to acquire AI underwriting and pricing software firm hyperexponential
item.description: With hx and Guidewire, insurers will be able to respond to submissions faster and, more importantly, improve loss ratios and allocate capital more effectively.” The post $1.7bn deal: Guidewire to acquire AI underwriting and pricing software firm hyperexponential appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Guidewire has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire hyperexponential (hx) for a base purchase price of $1.7bn in cash, subject to adjustments. Guidewire and hyperexponential are uniquely positioned to deliver industry-specific AI solutions that will transform commercial underwriting.
